questions.prompt: Forces of 60 N to the right and 25 N to the left act on a box. What is the resultant force?
questions.explain: Opposite forces subtract: 60 − 25 = 35 N, in the direction of the bigger force.

questions.prompt: A car moves along a straight road at a constant 20 m/s. What can you say about the forces on it?
options: There are no forces on the car
The forward force is bigger than the backward forces
They are balanced: the resultant force is zero
questions.explain: Constant velocity means no acceleration, so the resultant force must be zero.

feedback.1: A bigger forward force would make the car speed up.
feedback.0: Engine force, friction, air resistance and weight all act; they just balance.

questions.explain: Inertia depends on mass, not on speed. The truck has by far the most mass.

questions.prompt: A bus brakes suddenly. Why do standing passengers fall forwards?
options: Air rushes forwards inside the bus
Their bodies keep moving forwards because of inertia
questions.explain: The bus slows, but the passengers keep moving until a force (the floor, a pole) slows them too.

questions.prompt: A ball rolls across a carpet and stops. Which force stopped it?
options: Friction from the carpet (and air resistance)
No force: moving things stop naturally
The ball ran out of force
questions.explain: Objects only slow down when a resultant force acts against the motion.

feedback.1: That was Aristotle's idea; Newton showed that a force is needed to change motion.

questions.prompt: A 10 kg crate is pushed right with 50 N. Friction is 20 N. What is the resultant force (in N) to the right?
Sort each situation by the forces acting.

items.label: A book resting on a table
A plane cruising at a steady speed and height
A lift moving up at a constant speed
A car going round a bend at a steady speed

questions.explain: Constant velocity (including at rest) means balanced forces. Any change of speed OR direction means a resultant force.

questions.text: An object stays at ___ or keeps moving at a constant ___ unless a resultant ___ acts on it.
questions.explain: This is the law of inertia.

questions.prompt: Explain why a spacecraft travelling between planets does not need to keep its engines running.
questions.modelAnswer: In space there is almost no friction or air resistance, so there is no resultant force on the spacecraft (apart from gravity). By Newton's first law it keeps moving at the same velocity without any driving force. Engines are only needed to change its speed or direction.
rubric: No friction or air resistance in space
Newton's first law: no resultant force means constant velocity
Engines only needed to change velocity
questions.explain: Criterion A/D: applying the first law.
